The Grand Duchy Looks Ahead

Leopold II governs a grand duchy sustained by agriculture, workshops and the commerce of Livorno. His ministers continue a tradition of practical reform, while Austria remains the dynasty's protector. The court must decide which ambitions to cultivate. These are plans for the years ahead: any change of constitution, federation or Italian crown must still be won through later reforms and crises.
The Paternal Administration
Experienced officials sustain the public works and the ducal accounts.
Maintain the paternal administration.
Open the public accounts to municipal scrutiny.
The Legacy of Fossombroni

Fossombroni treats engineering and careful accounts as instruments of government. The reclamation works demand patience, and the cabinet must decide whether orderly administration will serve the court alone or make room for municipal scrutiny.
Close the journal and reassure Vienna.
Protect the journal under ordinary law.
The Antologia Question

The literary journal has become a meeting place for ideas that trouble Vienna. Its editors insist that intellectual exchange belongs to the Tuscan reform tradition, the court fears that political discussion will outrun its control.
Reorganised Tuscan Courts
Regular procedures improve the reach of the civil administration.
Give the courts a clear administrative hierarchy.
Require public proceedings and municipal representation.
The Reorganisation of the Courts
The civil and criminal courts are being reorganised. A clear hierarchy can make justice more predictable, while municipal advocates seek public procedures that restrain the officials themselves.
The Pisa Scientific Networks
Scholars exchange methods and build lasting connections between institutions.
Encourage scientific exchange.

The Congress of Italian Scientists

Pisa welcomes scholars from across the peninsula. Leopold attends an assembly devoted to science, yet the friendships formed in its halls also teach educated Italians to imagine a public larger than their separate states.
Entrust the programme to experienced administrators.
Invite Ridolfi and the moderate reformers into consultation.
The Old Governing Generation Passes

Fossombroni has died. Corsini and Cempini inherit an administration whose public works have become part of the dynasty's claim to rule. The next ministry must decide how far that practical reform tradition can accommodate a growing public voice.
Allow a lawful political press.
Permit discussion while preserving the palace police.
The Press Law of 1847

Leopold relaxes censorship as political expectations rise across Italy. Ridolfi argues that lawful public discussion can bind reform to the crown, the palace fears that concessions will be taken as permission to demand more.
Consult the municipalities and the established estates.
Make ministerial accounts answerable to the council.
The Consulta
The crown establishes a consultative council. Municipal reformers want ministers to answer to a public assembly, while hereditary patrons would keep advice separate from sovereignty.
Establish the guard under municipal officers.
Keep the guard under officers trusted by the crown.
The Civic Guard

A civic guard gives respectable citizens a place in public security. Its officers may support the government, but a guard that sees itself as the nation's representative will not obey every order from the palace.
Sign the preliminary arrangements.
Keep the discussions technical and consult Vienna.
The Preliminary Italian Customs League

Florence, Turin and Rome discuss common customs arrangements. The proposal promises easier commerce, but every court guards its revenues and political independence. An agreement on trade does not yet create a common government.
Promulgate the Statuto and summon the parliament.
Grant the statute while securing the palace administration.
The Tuscan Statuto

Leopold signs a statute establishing representative institutions and a restricted electorate. Ridolfi hopes to reconcile the dynasty with lawful Italian reform. The court can grant a constitution, but its survival will depend on the conduct of ministers, the army and the crown.
Send the Tuscan contingent to the national war.

Italy Cannot Be Bought With the Crown's Blood

The war between Sardinia and Austria asks Tuscany to choose between its dynastic protection and the national cause. Volunteers prepare to leave, while the palace weighs the danger of a complete rupture with Vienna.
The Students Held the Line
The volunteers' service links the army to Italian public life.
Honour the soldiers and the university volunteers.
Curtatone and Montanara

Tuscan troops and university volunteers hold their positions against the Austrian advance. Their sacrifice joins the duchy's military memory to the Italian cause, while bereaved households confront the cost of a war decided beyond Tuscany.

Prepare a lawful compromise with the democratic deputies.

The Democratic Ministry

Military disappointment and the collapse of moderate authority bring Montanelli and Guerrazzi into government. They call for a constituent settlement larger than the existing Statuto. The palace fears that the ministry will surrender the crown's remaining authority.
The provisional government must hold the country together.
Reconcile the statute and the crown before the breach becomes final.
The Triumvirate in Florence

Leopold has left Florence and sought refuge at Gaeta. Guerrazzi, Montanelli and Mazzoni form a provisional triumvirate. Their constituent project faces divisions at home and a dynasty that can still appeal to Austrian arms.
Austrian Occupation
The dynasty depends on Austrian protection, whose presence burdens its domestic standing.

The White Eagle Returns to Florence

Austrian intervention has restored the dynasty. Baldasseroni wants an orderly government capable of continuing the public works, while Maria Antonia and the court distrust the parliament. Protection from Vienna comes with political obligations that the country will remember.
Reconcile the Crown and the Statuto

Ridolfi and the municipalities offer to preserve the dynasty under a public constitutional settlement. Leopold must abandon government by personal command, and the democratic ministry must accept a lawful parliament.

The Tuscan Military Convention

Baldasseroni asks that Austrian protection support a permanent Tuscan training programme. Vienna must judge whether the allied dynasty should develop a more independent army. Consent establishes a reciprocal convention, refusal leaves the restored court without the proposed mission.

Retain the statute and reconcile the moderate administration.
The Crown and the Suspended Parliament

The parliament has not reconvened. The court proposes restoring personal government, while the moderate ministers defend representative institutions. Leopold can abolish the Statuto, retain a restricted chamber under royal ministers, or reconcile the crown with responsible constitutional government. The choice settles how Tuscany is governed without abandoning its Italian ambitions.

Give the House of Lorraine an Italian mission.
Retain the Austrian alliance while strengthening Tuscan independence.
Austria Leaves, but the Army Changes

The occupation troops leave Tuscany. Ferrari da Grado's reorganisation offers a practical foundation for a better army, but the country must choose whether its improved institutions serve continued dependence, an independent duchy or a larger Italian mission.
The grand duke leaves, Ricasoli forms a provisional government.
Rally the country around the crown and its public institutions.
The White Eagle will stand as an Italian ally of Vienna.

Ricasoli and Dolfi unite the moderates and the national movement against a court identified with Vienna. The army's loyalty is uncertain. A crown supported by effective institutions may survive, while an unprepared dynasty faces a provisional government committed to Turin.

The assembly has rejected restoration of the Lorraine government. Ricasoli presents union with Victor Emmanuel's constitutional monarchy as the means to complete the national settlement. A separate kingdom remains on the ballot, but the national movement has rallied around Turin.
